title: On most failed SWPC geomagnetic storm watch days in 2012-2026, the forecast CME or fast solar wind arrived, but the southward magnetic field was too weak for the watched storm level
abstract: NOAA SWPC geomagnetic storm watches state the highest G level for each of the next three days. An earlier campaign study found that watched days reached the watched level on only 19-30% of days. We found the source of these failures. For 805 watched days from September 2012 to July 2026 we took the forecast driver (CME, coronal-hole high-speed stream, or both) from the Rationale of SWPC's own 3-Day Forecast. We compared it with CME arrivals (Richardson and Cane ICME list, SWPC sudden impulses), OMNI solar-wind speed and IMF Bz, and GFZ Kp. The plan was written before the join. On 67% (95% block interval 62-72%) of the 571 failed days, the predicted structure was present on the day: a catalogued CME or wind of 500 km/s or more. On CME-watched days with a CME present, the watched level was reached on 85% of days with a lowest hourly Bz of -10 nT or less, and on 17% of other days. Watches found the arrival days: a CME was present on 55% of CME-watched days and on 9% of days with no watch. But after arrival, G1 occurred on 39% of CME-watched G1 days, near the 35% for all CME days. G2 and G3 watches picked stronger CMEs (33% and 22% reached, against 17% and 7% for all CME days), but most still failed. For CME watches, missing or mistimed arrivals were 63% of G1 failures, 36% of G2 and 28% of G3 failures. Thus a perfect arrival forecast would raise the reached rate only to about 0.39 (G1), 0.33 (G2) and 0.22 (G3). Reached-rate tables by level and stated driver, fitted on 2012-2019, gave no Brier gain on 2020-2026 over rates by level only (skill -1.4%, interval -5.1% to +2.3%). The low reached rate is mainly a geoeffectiveness limit: day-ahead forecasts do not know the field direction inside the arriving structure, so a stated probability near 0.3 describes the information in a watch better than a deterministic level. Limitations: catalogues can miss weak CMEs, driver labels come from keyword rules on SWPC text and are missing for 2019-02 to 2022-03, the analysis uses daily resolution, and G3+ cases are few. Code, parsed SWPC texts, per-day derived tables, figures and retrieval manifests are included; raw OMNI and Kp files stay external.
